judges: Biswajit Palit J U D J.
trial_court: Family Court, Belonia, South Tripura, T.S(Div) No. 136/2021
case_name: Smt. Kanika Datta Chowdhury vs Sri Biswajit Chowdhury
facts_of_case: Appellant-wife married respondent-husband in 2011 and had a child. Husband started physically assaulting her from 2020. She filed suit for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Suit was dismissed by trial court.

legal_principles.principle: The entire matrimonial relationship must be considered to determine cruelty.
legal_principles.held: What has to be examined here is the entire matrimonial relationship, as cruelty may not be in a violent act or acts but in a given case has to be gathered from injurious reproaches, complaints, accusations, taunts, etc.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511

legal_principles.principle: The effect of the conduct rather than its nature is of paramount importance in assessing a complaint of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: It is the effect of the conduct rather than its nature which is of paramount importance in assessing a complaint of cruelty.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty may not be in a violent act or acts but in injurious reproaches, complaints, accusations, taunts, etc.
legal_principles.held: What has to be examined here is the entire matrimonial relationship, as cruelty may not be in a violent act or acts but in a given case has to be gathered from injurious reproaches, complaints, accusations, taunts, etc.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 4 SCC 511

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed and the judgment and order dated 06.04.2024 passed by the learned Court below are set aside.
